correctness.rationale: The PBW basis 1,x,y,xy,y²,xy² is six-dimensional with a length-four radical filtration. For candidate images X,Y, the coefficient of y² in X² is b², forcing b=0. After ag≠0, all defining-relation residuals are scalar multiples of xy²: X²=ad(1+λ²)xy², Y³=fg²(1+λ+λ²)xy², YX−λXY=(λ−1)(aiλ−df(1+λ+λ²))xy². The Y³ equation kills the df term, leaving exactly three independent scalar constraints. Every satisfying pair defines an endomorphism surjective on the cotangent quotient; its induced associated-graded algebra map is surjective and finite radical length gives bijectivity. Hence these and only these automorphisms exist over any field. The exact free-coordinate count and reduced variety follow. Embedded verify.py exhaustively checks normalized coefficients for F2,F3,F4,F5 and independently checks selected full maps invertible; finite experiments do not replace the general proof.

value.rationale: The smallest asymmetric two-generator quantum complete intersection beyond the four-dimensional square-zero case is a natural testbed for how nilpotency exponents interact with skew commutation. This result completely determines its full automorphism locus and group size for every finite field and skew parameter, identifies genuinely distinct cubic-root and fourth-root mixing mechanisms, and explains the extra double jumps in characteristics 2 and 3. This is an infinite parameter-family classification with a structural necessity/sufficiency statement, not a routine fixed-example matrix count. The precise automorphism normal form is useful for subsequent orbit and module-classification problems, without claiming those downstream results.
